tickets.title: Delivery e-bike obstruction and fire risk on 11th Street
tickets.summary: Over 100 electric delivery bikes are stored on the sidewalk and street at 11th Street and 1st Avenue around the clock, which speakers say has closed businesses and blocked landlords from renting units. A speaker warned that the electric bikes "might pose a fire hazard, if, god forbid, something happens." The District Manager and the precinct have been working on the block since February 2024, and enforcement and bike confiscation are planned for October 7. Action: Ask the precinct and sanitation to provide a safe, translated warning and a workable plan for storing the bikes, and report back to the board on the enforcement.

tickets.title: Drug activity and dark areas in Seward Park
tickets.summary: Speakers and the Seward Park Conservancy and Lower East Side Ecology Center report increased drug use in Seward Park, including near a restroom used by drug users, and note that the park has poor lighting with dark spots. The precinct has stationed police in the park under a task force, and outreach providers already work there. Action: Ask the precinct and Parks Department to report on drug activity and lighting repairs in Seward Park and whether mobile crisis teams can be used there.

tickets.title: Manhattan Bridge exit safety and Canal Street update
tickets.summary: The committee's letter raised concerns about traffic at the foot of the Manhattan Bridge exits, citing a recent crash and death of a local resident there. The letter also asked for an update on the Canal Street redesign project, which has not had an update since January. Action: Follow up with the mayor and DOT on the Manhattan Bridge exit concerns and request the Canal Street redesign update.

tickets.title: Deny 11 Allen Street liquor license application
tickets.summary: The application for a full liquor license at 11 Allen Street, from an operator formerly of Time Cafe, was debated because the location is unlicensed, the area is saturated, and speakers cited crowds of about 150 people outside Time Cafe. The board voted to recommend denial of the full license, but the State Liquor Authority can still approve it without the board's stipulations. Action: Organize community members to attend the State Liquor Authority hearing and support the board's denial, and confirm the SLA calendar date.

tickets.title: Essex Market RFP postponement and community market
tickets.summary: The joint Land Use and Economic Development subcommittee met with EDC about the Essex Market RFP, which was due to go out at the end of the month. EDC did not clearly answer how the board's two resolutions were incorporated, so the board wants the RFP issuance postponed to keep the market community-run. Action: Hold the planned meeting with EDC and ask EDC to postpone the RFP until the board's resolutions are reflected in it.

tickets.title: Free public restrooms pilot in the district
tickets.location_raw: Delansancy and Suffach; Cooper Square at East Sixth Street and Third Avenue
tickets.summary: The city is installing two free public restrooms in the district as part of a one-year pilot, which DOT leads and a private contractor will keep clean. The committee raised concerns about access rules and emergency calls for the restrooms. Action: Pass a resolution at next month's meeting setting out the board's requests for the pilot period and send it to DOT.

tickets.title: Third Avenue L stop closure pilot
tickets.summary: A speaker analyzing MTA trip data argued that the L train stop at Third Avenue is mostly a waiting area, with only about 5% of riders boarding or leaving, and that closing it would save riders time. He asked the board to refer the idea to the transportation committee and to request a pilot closure with the MTA. Action: Refer the Third Avenue stop closure proposal to the transportation committee and ask the MTA about a pilot.

tickets.title: Community Board 3 mobile voting for CEC elections
tickets.summary: Parent Community Education Council elections have drawn turnout near 2%, and many households rely only on smartphones. The resolution asks the New York City public schools to pilot a mobile-first voting option that stays multilingual and accessible, alongside in-person voting, and to do more parent outreach that explains eligibility. Action: Vote on the resolution and send it to the Department of Education's family engagement office urging a pilot.

tickets.title: District needs statement and budget priorities vote
tickets.summary: The board will vote in October on its district needs statement and ranked expense and capital budget priorities for each city agency, based on committee work and meetings with about 20 agencies. The District Manager noted that the draft city housing plan proposes about 7,000 units over five years, but 75% are market rate, while affordable housing is the board's top need. Action: Finalize and vote on the district needs statement and ranked budget priorities in October, including the affordable housing comment.
